title: The lowest place (Luke 14:7–14)
hook: sit at the bottom of the table, and invite those who can't repay
carry: invite the ones who can't repay

segments.voice: Yesterday, a hen spread her wings over a city that wouldn't come. Your line was under her wings.

A wedding reception, and a seating chart on an easel by the door. Table one, near the couple: family and the best friends. Table twelve, by the kitchen door: the coworkers and the plus-ones nobody's met. And at least one guest quietly moves a place card. Jesus is at a sabbath dinner in the house of a leading Pharisee, watching the guests do exactly this: angling for the first seats. So he gives them some advice.
screen: `A SEATING CHART BY THE DOOR.` → `TABLE TWELVE, BY THE KITCHEN.` → `GUESTS ANGLING FOR THE BEST SEATS.`

segments.voice: First, to the guests. Don't grab the top seat, he says. Someone more honored may arrive, the host will ask you to move, and you'll walk the whole room to the bottom in front of everybody. "But when thou art invited, go, sit down in the lowest place." Then the host may say: friend, go up higher, and you'll be honored before the whole table. It sounds like good manners, and it is. The Book of Proverbs gives almost the same advice about standing before a king. But Jesus ends with a line that goes past manners: "every one that exalteth himself, shall be humbled; and he that humbleth himself, shall be exalted." Then he turns to the host. When you give a dinner, don't invite your friends, your brothers, your relatives or your rich neighbors, because they'll invite you back, and that's your repayment. Instead: "call the poor, the maimed, the lame, and the blind; And thou shalt be blessed, because they have not wherewith to make thee recompense." That's the harder half. You invite me, I invite you, and the account is settled. Jesus says: break the loop. Invite the people who can't pay you back, and let God do the repaying, at the resurrection of the just. The two halves fit. As a guest, don't measure your worth by your seat. As a host, don't measure your guests by what they can give. The lowest place isn't a trick for getting promoted. It's a way of sitting at a table where nobody is keeping score.
screen: `DON'T GRAB THE TOP SEAT.` · `FRIEND, GO UP HIGHER.` · `HE THAT HUMBLETH HIMSELF.` · `CALL THE POOR, THE LAME, THE BLIND.` · then, large: `SIT DOWN IN THE LOWEST PLACE.`

segments.voice: Think through today's rooms, a meeting, a meal, a line, a group chat, and where you'd usually take the better place: the first word, the best chair, the last slice, the credit. Picture taking the lower one instead, on purpose and quietly. If you pray, ask for a humble heart.
Last place. Jesus' advice at a dinner: take the bottom seat, and when you host, invite the ones who can't repay. Today's word.
Your line: invite the ones who can't repay. A seat at the table, and no account to settle. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Catholic parishes and communities, such as the Catholic Worker and the Community of Sant'Egidio, hold meals where the poor sit at the table as guests, not only as people being served food.

chat.says: Is "take the lowest seat" just a trick to get moved up higher?
options: No; it's sitting where nobody keeps score, and hosting people who can't repay.
Yes, it's clever manners: act humble so the host will honor you.
No; it means guests should always stand and never sit at a dinner.
chat.meaning: It isn't a trick for promotion: as a guest, don't measure your worth by your seat; as a host, invite those who can't repay.
